fields.companyDescription: Arbor Lodging (CALA) is the Caribbean & Latin America practice of Arbor Lodging—a vertically integrated hotel investment and management company. From a fully operational Mexico City base, we combine local presence with U.S. platform depth across business development, operations, sales, revenue management, marketing, finance, accounting, HR, and communications. We are an approved third-party operator for Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt, and IHG, with growing third-party management momentum in Mexico and the broader CALA region.
fields.brand_narrative_compliance: We balance brand standards with owner economics: proactive QA readiness, PIP execution, and joint decisions with ownership when renovation or revenue trade-offs arise—supported by experience implementing brand capital improvement guidelines across major flags.
fields.sustainabilityPrograms: No quantified sustainability program framework is specified in the ALM overview; initiatives are property and brand dependent.
fields.emergencyResponse: Crisis response is coordinated through local property teams and regional leadership with direct senior involvement.
fields.companyHistory: Arbor Lodging was founded in 2006 in Chicago by Vamsi Bonthala and Sheenal Patel as a vertically integrated hotel investment and management platform. The company operates Arbor Lodging Partners (investment) and Arbor Lodging Management (operations), with Arbor Management Solutions providing outsourced accounting and commercial support to other management companies. CALA expansion has been deliberate: a Mexico City office integrated with U.S. operations for several years, with Christian Hutchinson appointed Director of Business Development, CALA, in November 2025. This CALA Explorer profile should not be read as a current managed-hotel footprint claim for the region.

fields.owner_relevance: Shows Arbor can quickly stabilize and outperform in competitive urban markets through pricing discipline and commercial execution.
fields.services: Sophisticated revenue optimization by season/channel; enhanced F&B and meeting-space monetization; boutique-style guest experience positioning.
fields.outcome: Ranked #1 on TripAdvisor among 177 greater Phoenix hotels; total revenue +24.9% and GOP +24.1% (2024 vs 2022); #1 of 6 in RevPAR index growth in 2022 and 2023.

fields.owner_relevance: Demonstrates Arbor ability to execute complex historic repositioning with disciplined capex, brand-sensitive design, and measurable post-renovation performance lift.
fields.services: renovation planning and execution; F&B concept repositioning; hands-on revenue management and direct sales strategy.
fields.outcome: Renovation completed on-time and under budget; nearly 90% of invested capital returned in first 4 years (inclusive of tax credits); total revenue +23.4% and RevPAR index +11.0% (2024 vs 2023).

fields.owner_relevance: Highlights Arbor capability in complex independent resorts where owner value depends on integrated operations, capex sequencing, and revenue recapture.
fields.services: Comprehensive repositioning plan; amenity and F&B reprogramming; direct sales and revenue-management reset; local hands-on operating oversight.
fields.outcome: Early implementation already improving efficiency with upward RevPAR index and total revenue trends; NOI and value enhancement expected through phased renovations.

fields.owner_relevance: Demonstrates Arbor can execute live-hotel transition programs while improving index and margin performance during changeover.
fields.services: .2M public space/guestroom/back-of-house renovation; soft rebrand concepting; signature F&B launch; direct sales and revenue strategy.
fields.outcome: RevPAR index improved 300 bps in year 1 and another 300 bps in year 2; GOP margin rose from 36.7% to 39.8% in year 1; service continuity maintained during renovation.

fields.owner_relevance: Illustrates Arbor’s repeatable stabilization playbook for newly opened branded hotels that are not yet meeting potential.
fields.services: Guest-experience and operating-discipline program; revenue and cost structure optimization; cleanliness and maintenance performance reset.
fields.outcome: Revenue +10.5% and RevPAR index +9.0% in first year; GOP improved from 32.0% to 40.7% in first two years; significant brand-score improvement.

fields.owner_relevance: Validates Arbor’s ability to preserve and create value in distressed situations through operational fixes before heavy capital spend.
fields.services: Loan-to-own execution; foreclosure and transition management; cost-center restructuring; vendor renegotiation; sales strategy overhaul.
fields.outcome: EBITDA improved from - pre-ownership to break-even year 1 and + thereafter; exit generated 33% unleveraged IRR and 2.6x equity multiple.

fields.owner_relevance: Confirms Arbor can rapidly turn around branded select-service assets with measurable financial gains and compliance recovery.
fields.services: Detailed accountability action plan; dynamic pricing implementation; operating-cost discipline and guest-service resets.
fields.outcome: Revenue +12.6% in first year; RevPAR index +12.2% in first year; reached 49.0% GOP margin within first eight months; moved out of Marriott Red Zone in first wave.
